sections.heading: C — Vision and Health
sections.markdown:
## C — Vision and Health

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F01 | anchor: A01
Each driver bears personal responsibility for being in reasonably good health while driving [A01]
Why it matters: frames fitness to drive as an ongoing driver duty.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F02 | anchor: A01
A driver with a condition that may affect safe driving must report it and seek qualified health advice [A01]
Why it matters: self-reporting triggers proper evaluation before licensure.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F03 | anchor: A01
Health care professionals advising on driving fitness include doctors, physician assistants and advanced nurses [A01]
Why it matters: tells the applicant whose assessment the division accepts.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F04 | anchor: A01
A medical advisory board maintains driving fitness guidelines available through the division website [A01]
Why it matters: points candidates to the authoritative medical standard.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F05 | anchor: A01
The guidelines cover eleven health groups from metabolic and heart conditions through vision, strength and sleep [A01]
Why it matters: shows the breadth of conditions that can trigger review.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0030]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F06 | anchor: A02
Class D driving calls for at least twenty over forty vision in one eye plus at least ninety degrees of visual field [A02]
Why it matters: core eyesight threshold for regular passenger-car driving.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F07 | anchor: A02
A vision check is required at the field office and for applicants older than sixty-five at application [A02]
Why it matters: older first-time applicants should expect screening.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F08 | anchor: A02
Anyone unable to pass must carry an eye-exam certificate to an eye specialist and file acuity proof before approval [A02]
Why it matters: explains the referral path after a failed screening.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F09 | anchor: A02
Mental strain shows in anger at others, confusion in traffic, worry off the road, citations and grief reactions [A02]
Why it matters: links calm focus and extra travel time to staying safe.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F10 | anchor: A02
Some medicines bring drowsiness, so dosing must be arranged with a doctor and misuse of prescriptions avoided [A02]
Why it matters: medication effects count as impairment risks.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F11 | anchor: A02
Applicants answer health questions, may receive a mailed ability form for their clinician, and face possible limits or retesting [A02]
Why it matters: maps the paperwork route from disclosure to decision.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0031]

FACT_ID: sec05-vision-health-F12 | anchor: A03
A review exam may follow medical, police or citizen reports, and skipping it ends driving; a hearing officer then weighs needs, roads and medical guidance [A03]
Why it matters: review usually keeps driving with limits and ends it only when no safe condition exists.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0032]

Misconceptions: passing eyesight alone guarantees approval; review often allows limited driving when safe.
Mnemonic: Health Advises Vision Every Day for steady recall of duty, advice, sight, review and forms.
Glossary: fitness means safe ability; acuity means sharpness of sight; review means formal reassessment.
